governing_question: How do we turn sampled measurements into trustworthy, efficient decisions without confusing a mathematical model, a finite record, and a deployed signal chain?
assumptions: The course is planned for mathematically mature engineers who know calculus, complex arithmetic, basic probability, linear algebra, and ordinary programming, but do not yet have an integrated DSP mental model.

The 27-lesson pedagogical proposal supplies the teachable spine; four bounded advanced lessons—parametric spectra, minimum-phase/allpass structure, rigorous perfect-reconstruction banks, and wavelet/paraunitary banks—remain optional and never become prerequisites for the core path.
Formal sampling follows the DTFT so aliasing and reconstruction can be justified rather than asserted; this intentionally differs from the raw proposal order.

Oppenheim and Schafer dossier pointers use the locally researched Second Edition (1999), even though the initial canon label named the Third Edition; edition-specific page references must be reverified if the production team switches editions.

All 63 deduplicated image candidates with retained local captures are indexed; any item whose license is unknown, publisher-controlled, or third-party remains blocked on rights review and has a fallback to a drawn explanatory figure or rights-cleared measured artifact.

The five module-final applications require reproducible data, explicit units and parameters, quantitative thresholds, a falsification test, an idealization-gap statement, and a deliverable; external data acquisition and rights clearance remain production tasks.
Demo entries are contracts only: each specifies a variable target, threshold, and falsification behavior, and no demo component or lesson.mdx file is authored in this synthesis phase.

Every brief contains four to eight planned figures, four to eight exercises with no more than one mechanical item and at least two E6 items, and exactly one forward transfer; the final lesson uses the documented terminal-transfer exception.
